execution.progress: One stroke per paid round, at most 4 per segment; the work, the reserved piece, its end and the pinned abrasive persist.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds. inspect: 1 round, 0.5 energy; target an own wooden item or tool and/or x, y a soil point in reach. shape: target an own unreserved rigid wooden item; quantity in tenths (default the item, at most 1 unit, one piece); abrasive: a rigid inedible noncombustible surface in reach, e.g. a rock, or your own whole piece of it on firm ground; both pinned to one work (workId). Each stroke: 1 round, 1 energy; at most 4 per segment; resume continues paused work. maintain: the same strokes on your own shaped or broken tool. use: target your shaped tool; x, y a soil point in reach; load 0.05-1 (default 0.25); 1 round, 1 energy. quoteOnly true quotes shape or maintain free. pause, resume, cancel: no energy. Refusals cost nothing; failed rechecks pause work free. Travel and getting a stone are separate.
details.effects: A whole branch unit is a 0.04 m by 0.99 m green-wood rod; a piece is that part of it. A stroke is 100 passes; by the scratch rule a surface no harder than the other loses 0.0001 kg per pass, so the end loses up to 0.01 kg as dust beside you (piece plus dust equals input). The end tapers over 3 diameters; release needs a tip at most 0.35 diameter and a 0.3 m shaft (a whole branch: about 7 strokes). A shaped tool is unverified until a stroke moves soil. A use stroke presses and levers 30 times at load x 500 N: the tip enters forest or meadow soil until the soil resistance (higher when drier) bears it and moves up to 0.001 m3 of the patch's loose top 0.15 m into a heap beside it; rock, wet bank, waterlogged soil and water move 0. Ground contact wears 0.0001 kg off the tip. Above strength (hardness/10, half if split) the end splits, then breaks. Cancel returns the piece as it is; death leaves it at the worksite. No edge, fire, water, binding, gathering bonus or reward.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Propagate from seed
value.function: Crush one of your own whole berries and rub its seeds free by hand, inspect a planting site, and sow the seeds in a small hand-loosened patch where they may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; pause, resume or cancel sowing.
value.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.2 energy each. extract: target your own whole untreated berry item; one unit per attempt (quantity 1): 1 round, 0.5 energy. inspect: x, y a site in reach and/or target your own item or a sowing patch in reach: 1 round, 0.2 energy. sow: target your seed lot; x, y a site in reach on open ordinary soil (.), moisture 0.3-1.2, waterlogging at most 0.1, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 berry plants or patches being sown within 5 m. 2 rounds of 1 energy: loosen the patch, then place and cover the seeds; a loosened patch left by cancelled work needs only the second. pause, resume (workId), cancel: no energy. Refusals and failed rechecks cost nothing. No tool, vessel, water or soil is supplied.
value.effects: A whole berry unit (0.2 kg, food 8) is crushed: 0.01 kg of seeds (5 %, no food, no ageing) and 0.19 kg of pulp with all its food and age; both keep origin, harvest round and decay. The seeds of one unit are the one propagule the plant rules give one fruit unit; viability is unknown until something emerges. A unit whose parent is not a living berry plant has no represented seed: a paid failure, all pulp. Sowing moves the seeds from your inventory into the patch record, covered 5 mm deep in soil loosened 0.03 m. The patch gains establishment only from actual temperature (none at 6 C or below, full from 20 C), light, soil moisture (full from 0.6) and season; cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it. At 12 a rooted seedling appears with no fruit (stock at most 4, the parent plant interval); fruit grows only under the existing growth rule; anyone may gather it. Watering a rooted plant is rooted-plant-watering. An unworked round pauses; cancel returns unsown seeds once and leaves loosened soil; death leaves them where you died. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: extract and inspect take one round; sowing is two paid one-round phases whose work, reserved seeds and patch persist; resume pays only the remaining phase after rechecks; rooting and growth run only in ordinary simulation.

value.uncertainty: My tool's meadow penetration threshold and safe useful working load remain unknown; the forest comparison changes both tool and ground.
value.goal: Demonstrate soil displacement with a sound tool and record the tested conditions.
completedSteps: Inspected and shaped an owned branch.
value.missing: Successful personal displacement trial and post-stroke condition evidence.
value.next: Make one stroke at load 0.25 on the same meadow patch, then evaluate the reported condition and displacement.
value.benefit: The low-load trials establish limits under these meadow conditions, not yet a useful digging result.
